title: C++ meta kernel for sub.Tensor
body:

Python FakeTensorMode computes sub.Tensor metadata in Python. For symbolic
inputs it first tries make_fast_binary_impl(torch._refs.sub), and when that
bails out, or when the inputs are static, it runs torch._refs.sub, which
activate_meta registers as the Meta kernel. This adds sub_Tensor_meta, which
reproduces both paths in C++ on top of the add.Tensor helpers, so the
PyInterpreter fast-op callback can be removed for sub.

The fast path is shared with add unchanged: it ignores alpha and does no bool
check, like the Python fast impl. The ref differs from refs.add in three ways,
and binary_ref_meta takes an is_sub flag for them. After broadcasting, two bool
tensors raise NotImplementedError with the ref's message; Python numbers are
exempt. alpha is applied when alpha != 1 with Python equality, so 1.0 and True
count as 1 and a SymBool alpha never does. The check runs after broadcasting,
so a SymInt or SymFloat alpha guards Ne(alpha, 1) in the same order as the ref.
The alpha type check has no bool exemption. As in FakeTensorMode's
has_symbolic_sizes, only a SymInt alpha makes the call symbolic.

sub.Tensor gets `Meta: sub_Tensor_meta`. With the torchgen change from the add
commit, sub.out and sub_ keep their structured TensorIterator meta. On the
Python side, aten::sub.Tensor joins the activate_meta skip set and
_cpp_meta_supports_symint. The tests reuse the add harness, now parametrized by
op. They compare the C++ kernel with refs.sub (static) and the fast impl
(backed/unbacked) on sizes, strides, dtype, device and guards. They cover
layouts, broadcasting, promotion, alpha, the ref's errors, and SymInt and
SymFloat alphas that reach the ref.

Test Plan:

```
pip install -e . -v --no-build-isolation
python test/test_meta.py -k test_sub_meta
```

Regression suites, no new failures against the stack without these commits:

```
python -m pytest test/test_meta.py test/test_fake_tensor.py test/test_dynamic_shapes.py test/test_proxy_tensor.py test/dynamo/test_misc.py test/dynamo/test_dynamic_shapes.py
python -m pytest test/test_ops.py -k TestFakeTensor
python -m pytest test/test_decomp.py -k "add or sub or mul or div"
```
